items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to Order

items.evidence_text: PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
items.title: Public Communication

items.evidence_text: COUNTY ANNOUNCEMENTS
items.title: County Announcements

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation honoring Commissioner Margaret Gómez for her 
extraordinary service to Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Proclamation Honoring Commissioner Margaret Gómez

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve Payment of Claims

items.evidence_text:
3. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to Travis County’s 
response, operations, policies, emergency assistance, agreements, and 
measures necessary to preserve public health and safety and 
rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, declarations or 
resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds and contracts 
related to disaster response and recovery efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Emergency Services Matters

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the Consent by Lien Holder, for 
Travis County Facilities Corporation, a Texas public facility corporation, to grant 
an electric utility easement to the City of Austin, on that property being described 
as 11.58 acres, more or less, consisting of that certain parcel stated to contain 
6.60 acres, more or less, and that certain parcel stated to contain 4.98 acres, 
more or less, being a portion of Outlot 28 and Outlot 31, Division A, Government 
Outlots adjoining the original City of Austin, and being a portion of Lot 1, 
Siegmund Addition, Section Four, a subdivision of Travis County, Texas; and is 
the same property which received legal lot status in City of Austin Case C81-
2026-0137 attached to the Electric Utility Easement, being the same property 
described in that certain Special Warranty Deed recorded in Document No. 
2024130246. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Approve Consent by Lien Holder for Electric Utility Easement

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve an amendment to the 
Community Development Block Grant COVID-19 (“CDBG-CV”) Response 
Project subrecipient agreement for the Sunrise Homeless Navigation Center 
(“SUN”) – Sunrise Homeless Response Initiative. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Amend Community Development Block Grant COVID-19 Agreement

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action to approve modification to Interlocal 
Agreement No. 4600001072 with Worksource – Greater Austin Area Workforce 
Board DBA Workforce Solutions – Capital Area Workforce Board, for the 
provision of Child Care Scholarships (Judge Brown & Commissioner Shea).
items.title: Modify Interlocal Agreement for Child Care Scholarships

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action to approve modification to Interlocal 
Agreement No. 4600001073 with Worksource – Greater Austin Area Workforce 
Board DBA Workforce Solutions – Capital Area Workforce Board, for the 
provision of Child Care Gap Funding Payments Program . (Judge Brown & 
Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Modify Interlocal Agreement for Child Care Gap Funding

items.evidence_text:
8. Receive a briefing on two reports produced by the Research & Planning Division 
of HHS: the Travis County Snapshot from the 2024 American Community 
Survey and the Fiscal Year 2025 Community Impact Report. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Briefing on HHS Reports

items.evidence_text:
9. Consider and take appropriate action on a request to approve Environmental 
Exemptions for the following projects/activities that will receive Community 
Development Block Grant (CDBG) and/or HOME funding during Program Year 
2025 (PY25) from HUD: 
    
  A. Program Year 2025 Administration & Planning (CDBG) 
  B. Program Year 2025 HOME Program 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve Environmental Exemptions for HUD-Funded Projects

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on the following grant Letters of Intent, 
contracts and related special budgets, and permissions to continue: 
    
  A. Any other necessary grant applications, letters of support or grant awards 
attached to Commissioners Court backup for this Agenda item 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Grant Letters of Intent, Contracts, and Permissions

items.evidence_text:
11. Consider and take appropriate action on an appointment to the Strategic 
Housing Finance Corporation Board of Directors. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Appointment to Strategic Housing Finance Corporation Board

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action on an appointment to the Animal Advisory 
Commission. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Appointment to Animal Advisory Commission

items.evidence_text:
13. Consider and take appropriate action on an appointment to the Sobering Center 
Board of Directors. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Appointment to Sobering Center Board

items.evidence_text: 14. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Authorize Investment of County Funds

items.evidence_text:
15. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
Afterschool Youth Enrichment Fund (0149) of $6,187.50 for revenue 
received by Health and Human Services related to the AmeriCorps 
Formula Grant for the CAPITAL AmeriCorps Project 
  B. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a New Budget of 
$4,300 for Revenue Received from Reliant Energy for the CARE 
Program 
  C. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
the Bluebonnet Electric Fund (2112) of $12,000 for revenue received by 
Health and Human Services related to the Bluebonnet Electric 
Cooperative 
  D. Request from the Travis County Sheriff's Office to add one vehicle to the 
County's fleet which will be purchased from the Office's Inmate Welfare 
Funds 
  E. Request from the Facilities Management Department (FMD) for 
$4,780,050 from a $13,040,000 Capital Improvement Plan Earmark 
against the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve to complete 
work on prioritized projects 
  F. Request from the Technology and Operations Department (TOPS) for a 
total of $703,831 from the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve 
that include $440,565 for the replacement and purchase of Automated 
External Defibrillators (AEDs) across Travis County facilities and the use 
of $263,266 from a $350,000 Earmark Against the CAR Reserve for 
Constable vehicle AEDs with the remaining Earmark of $86,734 to be 
released 
  G. Request from Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within the Technology 
and Operations Department (TOPS) for $1,756,018 from the Fiscal Year 
2026 Catastrophic Loss Reserve within the Risk Management Fund 
(8955) to cover short-term liabilities for the remainder of the Fiscal Year 
  H. Request from the Juvenile Probation Department to reallocate $416,748 
from the air handler project that was included as part of the Fiscal Year 
2026 Adopted Budget and has a current balance of $534,748. These 
funds will now be used for critical fire panel safety repairs needed in 
Fiscal Year 2026. The Department will request these funds and 
additional funds as part of the Fiscal Year 2027 budget process to 
complete the air handler project 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Budget Amendments and Transfers

items.evidence_text:
16. Receive briefing from PBO as directed by Commissioners Court on potential 
options for changes to Longevity Pay for Fiscal Year 2027. (Commissioner 
Shea)
items.title: Briefing on Longevity Pay Options

items.evidence_text:
17. Consider and take appropriate action on the draft Travis County Foreign Trade 
Zone Policy and Guidelines for Consideration of Requests for Support for site 
activation. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider Travis County Foreign Trade Zone Policy

items.evidence_text: 18. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive Bids from Purchasing Agent

items.evidence_text:
19. Approve contract award for professional consulting services, Slaughter Lane 
East Median Improvement, RFQ No. 2209-005-TL, in the amount of 
$164,191.76, to the most highly qualified respondent, Kimley-Horn and 
Associates, Inc. (Transportation & Natural Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for Slaughter Lane Consulting

items.evidence_text:
20. Approve contract award for professional engineering services, Pace Bend Park 
Well Installation, RFQ No. 2209-005-TL, in the amount of $148,170.90, to the 
most highly qualified respondent, Martinez, Wright & Mendez, Inc., dba MWM 
DesignGroup, Inc. (Transportation & Natural Resources) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for Pace Bend Park Engineering

items.evidence_text:
21. Approve contract award for Generators Preventative Maintenance and 
Servicing, IFB No. 192-SM, to the following low bidders: 
    
  A. Contract No. 4400008764 with JPEC Services, LLC, in the amount of 
$184,435.00 
  B. Contract No. 4400008748 with Allegiant Generator Services NA LLC, in 
the amount of $15,920.00 (Juvenile Probation Department and Travis 
County Sheriff's Office)  
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for Generator Maintenance

items.evidence_text:
22. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400008126 with NIKSUN, Inc, in 
the amount of $96,889.00, for Network Analytics Tool. (Technology & 
Operations) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Modification for Network Analytics Tool Contract

items.evidence_text:
23. Approve Modification No. 1, an assignment of Contract No. 4400002753, for 
Braker Lane North Roadway Extension, from CP&Y Inc. to STV Incorporated. 
(Transportation & Natural Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Assignment of Braker Lane Roadway Extension Contract

items.evidence_text:
24. Approve contract award for professional engineering services, 700 Lavaca 
Generator Replacement MEP, RFQ No. 2209-005-TL, in the amount of 
$122,000.00, to the most highly qualified respondent, IMEG Consultants Corp. 
(Facilities Management Department) (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for 700 Lavaca Generator Replacement

items.evidence_text:
25. Approve ratification of Modification No. 5 to Contract No. 4400006723 with 
Austin/Travis County Reentry Roundtable, in the amount of $35,000.00, for 
community engagement for formerly incarcerated persons. (Innovative Justice & 
Program Analysis) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Ratification of Reentry Roundtable Contract Modification

items.evidence_text:
26. Approve contract award for professional consulting services, Third Party Review 
of County Development and/or Transportation Permit Applications, RFQ No. 
2209-005-TL, in the amount of $500,000.00, to the most highly qualified 
respondent, SE3, LLC. (Transportation and Natural Resources) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for Third Party Permit Review Services

items.evidence_text:
27. Approve Modification No. 1, an assignment of Contract No. 4400006626, for 
Appraisal Services, from Edward B Schulz & Co LLC dba Integra Realty 
Resources – Houston to North American Valuation and Consulting LLC dba 
Integra Realty Resources – Houston. (Transportation & Natural Resources) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Assignment of Appraisal Services Contract

items.evidence_text:
28. Approve contract award for car washing services, RFS 171-PE, as needed, to 
the sole respondent, The Car Wash Group, LLC dba Mr. Sharky’s Car Wash. 
(Transportation & Natural Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Contract Award for Car Washing Services

items.evidence_text:
29. Approve order exempting the purchase of The WRAP Restraint System from 
Safe Restraints, Inc., as needed, from the competitive procurement process, 
pursuant to County Purchasing Act § 262.024(a)(2) and authorize Purchasing 
Agent to issue purchase orders. (Sheriff’s Office) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Exemption for Purchase of WRAP Restraint System

items.evidence_text:
30. Consider and take appropriate action on the following Personnel Amendments: 
    
  A. Routine Personnel Actions 
  B. Non-Routine Personnel Actions 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Personnel Amendments

items.evidence_text:
31. Consider and take appropriate action on the annual approved County Holiday 
Schedule, effective October 1, 2026, through December 31, 2027. 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: County Holiday Schedule Approval

items.evidence_text:
32. Consider and take appropriate action on a license agreement with Texas Law 
Austin for their Summer Social Event on June 2, 2026, from 3:00pm – 8:00pm, 
on the 12th floor at the Civil and Family Courts Facilities, located at 1700 
Guadalupe Street, Austin, Texas 78701. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: License Agreement for Texas Law Austin Social Event

items.evidence_text:
33. Consider and take appropriate action regarding a lease with the Health and 
Human Services Commission for Travis County to use 1,183 square feet in 
Building 784 of the Austin State Hospital Campus, located at 4110 Guadalupe 
Street in Austin, Texas. Facilities Management is requesting to have the 
Commissioner’s Court delegate authority to approve yearly renewals to the 
Director of Facilities Management to sign subsequent site-specific environmental 
reviews. (Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Lease with Health and Human Services Commission

items.evidence_text:
34. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the allocation of office space at 
the Travis County Administration Building, 700 Lavaca, Austin, Texas 78701 as 
follows: 
    
  A. Commissioner of Precinct 1 to move from Suite 2.200 on the 2nd floor 
and be allocated space in Suite 1510 on the 15th floor 
  B. Commissioner of Precinct 4 to move from Suite 1510 on the 15th floor 
and be allocated space in Suite 2.200 on the 2nd floor 
(Judge Brown & Commissioner Traviliion)
items.title: Office Space Allocation at 700 Lavaca

items.evidence_text:
35. Consider and take appropriate action on the Amended Vehicle Replacement 
Policy. (Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Amended Vehicle Replacement Policy

items.evidence_text:
36. Consider and take appropriate action regarding a request to use a Cash 
Security Agreement for environmental fiscal security for AAA Storage Priem 
Lane Phase Two (Gattis School), in Precinct One. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Cash Security Agreement for AAA Storage Priem Lane Phase Two

items.evidence_text:
37. Consider and take appropriate action on the Fifth Amendment to the 
Construction Agreement between Rastegar Related Fund Management Infinity 
Park Property Owner L, RPC F1 Once LLC, and Travis County for the McAngus 
Industrial Development project, in Precinct Four. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Fifth Amendment to McAngus Industrial Development Construction Agreement

items.evidence_text:
38. 
Approve setting a public hearing on July 7, 2026, regarding a request to 
authorize the filing of an instrument to vacate a public utility easement located 
along the lot lines of Lots 408 & 873, Apache Shores Section 2, a subdivision in 
Precinct Three. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Set Public Hearing for Utility Easement Vacation

items.evidence_text:
39. Consider and take appropriate action on the Construction and Traffic Mitigation 
Agreement between Sunfield Development LLC, Sunfield Investments LLC, and 
Travis County for traffic mitigation associated with the proposed Sunfield 
development, in Precinct Four. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Traffic Mitigation Agreement for Sunfield Development

items.evidence_text:
40. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4 & 6 (Commissioner Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Executive Session: Security Issues

items.evidence_text:
41. Receive update on IJPA County Executive Recruitment in executive session.1&3 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Executive Session: IJPA Recruitment

items.evidence_text:
42. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action on letter of intent for solar 
leases with PowerFin Partners.1&2 (Judge Brown)
items.title: Executive Session: Solar Lease Legal Briefing

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn

emergency assistance, agreements, preparedness for future flood events 
and other disasters, and measures necessary to preserve public health 
and safety and rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, 
declarations or resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds 
and contracts related to disaster response, preparedness and recovery 
efforts
items.title: Manage outdoor burning and emergency disaster response

items.evidence_text:
3. Conduct interview of candidates for Director of Emergency Management and 
take appropriate action (This item may be taken into Executive Session under 
Government Code section 551.074, Personnel Matters exception, and 
Government Code section 551.071, Consultation with Attorney exception).
items.title: Interview and appoint Director of Emergency Management

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action to approve Subaward modification No. 3 to 
Contract No. 4400007239 with El Buen Samaritano Episcopal Mission. (Judge 
Brown & Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Modify subaward contract with El Buen Samaritano Episcopal Mission

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the Emergency Food 
Assistance Program (TEFAP) Contracting Entity and Site Agreement (Judge 
Brown & Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Approve Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP) agreement

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action on any necessary grant applications, 
letters of support or grant awards attached to Commissioners Court backup for 
this Agenda item. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Review and approve intergovernmental grant applications and awards

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action on the appointment of Pedro Villalobos to 
the Board of Directors of the Austin Dispute Resolution Center. (Commissioner 
Morales)
items.title: Appoint Pedro Villalobos to Austin Dispute Resolution Center Board

items.evidence_text: 8. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Authorize investment of county funds

items.evidence_text:
9. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item:
items.title: Process budget amendments and transfers

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on request from the District Judges for 
flexibility to set the Travis County Auditor’s compensation as set forth and 
authorized in the Order of the District Judges and Local Government Code 
§152.032. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Set compensation for Travis County Auditor

items.evidence_text: 11. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive county purchasing bids

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action to establish an interlocal agreement 
between Travis County and the City of Austin to collaborate on history projects 
and initiatives. (Commissioners Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Establish interlocal agreement for history projects

items.evidence_text:
13. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the First Amendment of the 
Memorandum of Understanding between Travis County and the Travis County 
Parks Foundation, extending the term of the agreement from September 14, 
2026, through September 13, 2031. (Commissioner Howard & Morales)
items.title: Approve amendment to Memorandum of Understanding with Travis County Parks Foundation

items.evidence_text:
14. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the approval of one (1) 
Agricultural Lease Amendments on Parks/Open Space. (Commissioner 
Morales)
items.title: Approve agricultural lease amendment for park lands

items.evidence_text:
15. Consider and take appropriate action regarding a temporary detour and 
restriction of all traffic on Old San Antonio Road and Puryear Road beginning on 
or about Wednesday, September 16, 2026, and continuing through Sunday, 
March 14, 2027, or until work is complete, in Precinct Three. (Commissioner 
Howard)
items.title: Authorize temporary traffic detour on Old San Antonio Road and Puryear Road

items.evidence_text:
16. Consider and take appropriate action to amend the Interlocal Agreement 
between the City of Austin and Travis County for consultant services to renew 
the US Fish and Wildlife Service Incidental Take Permit (#TE788841-2) and the 
Balcones Canyonlands Conservation Plan. (Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Amend interlocal agreement with City of Austin for conservation permitting

items.evidence_text:
17. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4 & 6 (Commissioner Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Briefing on security and information security issues

items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to Order

items.evidence_text: PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
items.title: Public Communication

items.evidence_text: COUNTY ANNOUNCEMENTS
items.title: County Announcements

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation recognizing September 24, 2026 as Cathy McHorse 
Day in Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Proclamation Recognizing Cathy McHorse Day

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Payment of Claims

items.evidence_text:
3. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to the disaster or 
emergency, including Travis County’s response, operations, policies, 
emergency assistance, agreements, preparedness for future flood events 
and other disasters, and measures necessary to preserve public health 
and safety and rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, 
declarations or resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds 
and contracts related to disaster response, preparedness and recovery 
efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Emergency Services Matters

items.evidence_text:
4. Approve setting a public hearing on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, to consider and 
take appropriate action, as well as receive comments regarding the issuance of 
an outdoor music festival permit and a mass gathering permit for the Seismic 9.0 
Dance Event, to be held on November 13-15, 2026, at 8509 Burleson Rd, 
Austin, TX 78719. (Judge Brown & Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Set Public Hearing for Outdoor Music Festival and Mass Gathering Permits

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve modification to Interlocal 
Agreement No. 4600001073 with Worksource – Greater Austin Area Workforce 
Board DBA Workforce Solutions – Capital Area Workforce Board, for the 
provision of Child Care Gap Funding Payments Program (Judge Brown & 
Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Modification to Child Care Gap Funding Payments Agreement

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action to approve modification to Interlocal 
Agreement No. 4600001072 with Worksource – Greater Austin Area Workforce 
Board DBA Workforce Solutions – Capital Area Workforce Board, for the 
provision of Child Care Scholarships. (Judge Brown & Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Modification to Child Care Scholarships Agreement

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action to approve a modification to Professional 
Services Subaward with Ascension Seton, Contract No.4600000841, for the 
provision of Hospital-Based Violence Intervention Services. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Modification to Hospital-Based Violence Intervention Services Agreement

items.evidence_text:
8. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the renewal and modification to 
Interlocal Agreement No. 400001753 with Integral Care to fund the Community 
Advancement Network. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Renewal and Modification of Integral Care Agreement

items.evidence_text:
9. Consider and take appropriate action on the following grant Letters of Intent, 
contracts and related special budgets, and permissions to continue: 
    
  A. Award Agreement for the Fiscal Year 2027 Other Victim Assistance 
Grant from the Office of the Attorney General for Travis County 
Attorney's Office 
  B. Award Agreement for the Fiscal Year 2027 Comprehensive Underage 
Drinking Prevention Program from the Texas Department of 
Transportation for the Travis County Attorney's Office 
  C. Award Agreement for the Fiscal Year 2027 Comprehensive STEP from 
the Texas Department of Transportation for the Travis County Sheriff's 
Office 
  D. Award Agreement for the Fiscal Year 2026 Formula Grant from the 
Texas Indigent Defense Commission for the Travis County Criminal 
Courts 
  E. Application from Travis County Innovative Justice and Program Analysis 
for the Fiscal Year 2026 Smart Reentry Demonstration Program solicited 
by the Bureau of Justice Assistance 
  F. Any other necessary grant applications, letters of support or grant awards 
attached to Commissioners Court backup for this Agenda item 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Grant Letters of Intent, Contracts, and Related Budgets

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on appointments to the Travis County 
Children's Protective Services Board to: 
    
  A. Designate board positions and expiration terms for Chris Craft, Anita 
Daniels, and Morgan Davis who were appointed on August 11, 2026 
  B. Reappoint Kelley Fowler and Lindsay Spinney to terms that will expire on 
June 30, 2029 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Appointments to Children's Protective Services Board

items.evidence_text:
11. Consider and take appropriate action to approve a lease agreement with 
Westlake Bible Church, Inc., also known as Austin Ridge Bible Church, for the 
Travis County Sheriff's Office Drone Unit to use designated facilities for training 
purposes at no cost to the County. (Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Lease Agreement for Sheriff's Office Drone Unit Training

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action for No-Cost Renewal of the ILA between 
Travis County and the Dell Medical School. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: No-Cost Renewal of ILA with Dell Medical School

items.evidence_text:
13. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the First Amendment and First 
Renewal to the Fiscal Year 2026 Interlocal Agreement with the City of Austin for 
Intake and Related Services at the Travis County Central Intake Facility and 
Criminal Justice Center. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Interlocal Agreement with City of Austin for Intake Services

items.evidence_text:
14. Approve declaration and resolution to establish the Felony Mental Health 
Diversion Court as a Mental Health Program pursuant to Texas Government 
Code, Chapters 121 and 125. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Establishment of Felony Mental Health Diversion Court

items.evidence_text: 15. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Investment of County Funds

items.evidence_text:
16. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request by Transportation & Natural Resources to establish a new 
budget totaling $358,859.50, comprised of $19,241.25 in the BCP Fund 
(0115) from a damage settlement, $228,898 in Fund 5000 for Parkland 
Fees, and $110,720.25 in Fund 5001 for Traffic Mitigation Fees 
  B. Request from the Planning and Budget Office to transfer $3,465 from the 
Allocated Reserve to General Administration to cover remaining External 
Auditor invoices 
  C. Request from Health & Human Services to Establish a New Budget in 
Fund 2034 of $4,747.62 for Revenue Received by Health & Human 
Services Related to the Texas Gas Service – Share the Warmth Program 
  D. Request from Pretrial Services to transfer $100,000 from the Allocated 
Reserve, which includes the remaining $23,803 from a $500,000 
Earmark against the Allocated Reserve to cover additional anticipated 
expenditures for court mandated Electronic Monitoring Devices for the 
remainder of Fiscal Year 2026 
  E. Request from Risk Management within the Technology and Operations 
Department (TOPS), and the County Auditor's Office to transfer 
$1,615,777 from the FY 2026 Catastrophic Loss Reserve within the Risk 
Management Fund (8955) needed for the actuarial liabilities entry to 
assist with Fiscal Year 2026 year-end close for the fund 
  F. Request from the County Attorney’s Office for $60,000 from the Allocated 
Reserve related to outside counsel legal fees for the District Attorney’s 
Office approved by Commissioners Court on July 28, 2026, Item 39 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Budget Amendments and Transfers

items.evidence_text:
17. Consider and take appropriate action on remaining Fiscal Year 2027 Budget 
issues, including: 
    
  A. Changes After Markup List 
  B. Other Remaining Items 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Issues

items.evidence_text:
18. Consider and take appropriate action on proposed Fiscal Year 2027 Budget 
Rules. (Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Rules

items.evidence_text: 19. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive Bids

items.evidence_text:
20. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400006381 with Marmon Mok, LP, 
in the amount of $72,074.00, for West Service Center New Fleet Building 
Design. (Facilities Management Department) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: West Service Center New Fleet Building Design Contract

items.evidence_text:
21. Approve exemption and Contract No. 4400008033 with Neuropsychology 
Specialists of Austin, PLLC, as needed, for neuropsychologist services. 
(Juvenile Probation Department) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Neuropsychologist Services Contract

items.evidence_text:
22. Approve Modification No. 5 to Contract No. 4400002551 with John Matthew 
Fabian, PSYD, JD, LLC, as needed, for Psychological/ Psychiatric Services. 
(Criminal Courts) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Psychological/Psychiatric Services Contract

items.evidence_text:
23. Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400002685 with Hilltop Securities 
Inc., an as-needed contract, for services. (Planning and Budget Office) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Hilltop Securities Contract Modification

items.evidence_text:
24. Approve termination of Contract No. 4400008585 with Reverse Training 
Program LLC, for Commercial Driver's License Training. (Innovative Justice & 
Program Analysis) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Termination of Commercial Driver's License Training Contract

items.evidence_text:
25. Approve Modification No. 14 to Contract No. 4400003950 with Capital Area 
Private Defender Service (CAPDS), in the amount of $1,486,908.00, for 
Forensic Review Project. (Community Legal Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Forensic Review Project Contract Modification

items.evidence_text:
26. Approve Modification No. 30, to Contract No. 4400001068, with i3-ImageSoft, 
LLC, in the amount of $57,500.00, for Imaging and Document Management 
System and Maintenance. (Technology and Operations) (Commissioners 
Travillion)
items.title: Imaging and Document Management System Contract

items.evidence_text:
27. Approve Modification No. 10 to Contract No. 4400004276 with Capital Area 
Private Defender Service (CAPDS), in the amount of $4,243,801.00, for 
Management of Assigned Counsel (MAC). (Community Legal Services) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Management of Assigned Counsel Contract Modification

items.evidence_text:
28. Authorize the Purchasing Agent to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for CDL 
Training Services for clients enrolled in the Innovative Justice and Program 
Analysis Reentry Resources program. (Justice Planning) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Request for Proposal for CDL Training Services

items.evidence_text:
29. Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction pursuant to Local 
Government Code § 263.152(a)(1). (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Surplus Property Auction

items.evidence_text:
30. Approve order exempting the purchase of 96-month inspection services from 
Leonardo Helicopters US Corporation, estimated requirements, from the 
competitive procurement process, pursuant to County Purchasing Act Section 
§262.024(a)(2) and §262.024(a)(11) and authorize Purchasing Agent to issue 
purchase orders. (Emergency Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Exemption for Helicopter Inspection Services

items.evidence_text:
31. Approve Modification No. 4 to Contract No. 4400006260 with Aeschbach & 
Associates, Inc., dba Addiction and Psychotherapy Services, in the amount of 
$75,000.00, for methadone treatment services. (Health & Human Services) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Methadone Treatment Services Contract Modification 1

items.evidence_text:
32. Approve Modification No. 4 to Contract No. 4400006261 with Community 
Medical Services, in the amount of $75,000.00, for methadone treatment 
services. (Health & Human Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Methadone Treatment Services Contract Modification 2

items.evidence_text:
33. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400006700 with Communities for 
Recovery, in the amount of $175,000.00, for overdose prevention services. 
(Health & Human Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Overdose Prevention Services Contract Modification

items.evidence_text:
34. Declare the list of Travis County equipment as missing and authorize removal 
from the SAP Asset Inventory, pursuant to Purchasing and Procedures Guide § 
22.003. (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Declare Equipment Missing

items.evidence_text:
35. Consider and take appropriate action on the following Personnel Amendments: 
    
  A. Routine Personnel Actions 
(Commissioners Travillion & Morales)
items.title: Personnel Amendments

items.evidence_text:
36. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the license agreement between 
Travis County and the TEX-ABOTA Best in Texas to use Travis County 
courtrooms for a Voir Dire Competition at the Civil and Family Courts Facility. 
(Commissioner Howard)
items.title: License Agreement for Voir Dire Competition

items.evidence_text:
37. Consider and take appropriate action on issuing an open call for 
recommendations on naming the Southeast Metropolitan Park, in accordance 
with provisions in the Travis County Code 1.021 and for the Commissioners 
Court to receive public comment and take appropriate action on September 29, 
2026. (Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Naming Southeast Metropolitan Park

items.evidence_text:
38. Consider and take appropriate action regarding Election Day polling locations for 
the November 3, 2026 Joint General and Special Elections. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Election Day Polling Locations

items.evidence_text:
39. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the Early Voting polling locations 
for the November 3, 2026 Joint General and Special Elections. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Early Voting Polling Locations

items.evidence_text:
40. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the Public Defender's Office 
use of departmental funds on an ongoing basis to maintain a coffee station and 
healthy snack food pantry for the department's indigent clients in accordance 
with the Travis County Non-Travel Meals and Related Expenditures Policy. 
(Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Public Defender Office Coffee and Snack Station

items.evidence_text:
41. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the Joint Election Agreement for 
the November 3, 2026 Joint General and Special Elections and December 12, 
2026 Joint Runoff Elections, if a runoff election is needed. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Joint Election Agreement

items.evidence_text:
42. Consider and take appropriate action on Urban Empowerment Zone I, LLC 
(Supportive Housing Initiative Project, Contract Number 4600001020, with the 
Leasehold Deed of Trust with Security Agreement and Assignment of Rents, 
recorded in Document NO. 2025057539 of the Official Public Records of Travis 
County, Texas) request for Travis County as lien holder to execute two Lien 
Holder Consents for 1.013 Acres Out of Tract Three, one as to the Declaration 
of a Drainage Easement and Unified Development Agreement with Maintenance 
of Drainage Facilities Restrictive Covenant and one as to a Drainage Easement, 
each granted by Travis County Facilities Corporation as described in the 
documents, with the City of Austin as grantee. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Lien Holder Consent for Drainage Easements

items.evidence_text:
43. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4&6 (Commissioners Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Security and Information Security Issues

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn

Listed below are bids, purchase orders, contracts, and other items to be approved under the Consent Agenda (Agenda Items A - GG).  This listing is provided on the Consent Agenda to allow Council Members to discuss or withdraw an item prior to approval of the Consent Agenda.  If no items are pulled, Consent Agenda Items A - GG below will be approved with one motion.  If items are pulled for separate discussion, they may be considered as the first items following approval of the Consent Agenda.
A.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City Council of the City of Denton, Texas, approving a grant application from Brandon Martino, representing RLB Investments, LLC, from the Downtown Reinvestment Grant Program not to exceed $25,000; and providing for an effective date.  The Downtown Task Force recommends approval (14-0). The Economic Development Partnership Board recommends approval (3-2).
B.
Consider approval of a resolution of the City Council of the City of Denton, Texas, appointing a Primary Member as an official voting representative to the North Central Texas Council of Governments Regional Transportation Council ("RTC"); and providing an effective date.
C.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas restricting parking on both sides of Wainwright Street from its intersection with Prairie Street to its intersection with Sycamore; providing a repealer clause; providing a savings clause; providing for a penalty not to exceed $500 for violations of this ordinance; providing that violations of this ordinance shall be governed by Chapter 18 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Denton; and providing for an effective date.
D.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas adding Section 18-38 of the Code of Ordinances relating to the use of wireless communication devices while driving; by creating Section 18-38 to prohibit the use of wireless communication devices while operating a motor vehicle except for dialing a number or talking to another person with certain defenses, providing a repealer clause; proving a savings clause; providing for a penalty not to exceed $200 for violations of this ordinance, and providing for an effective date.
E.
Consider approval of a resolution by the City of Denton, Texas, authorizing the City Manager to sign and submit to the Department of Housing and Urban Development a 2014 Action Plan for Housing and Community Development with appropriate certifications, as authorized and required by the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended, and the National Affordable Housing Act of 1990, as amended; and providing for an effective date.
F.
Consider adoption of an ordinance authorizing the City Manager to execute a Cooperative Purchasing Program Agreement with the City of Weatherford, Texas under Section 271.102 of the Local Government Code, to authorize City of Denton contracts for the purchase of various goods and services; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; and declaring an effective date (File 5528-Cooperative Purchasing Program Agreement with the City of Weatherford).
G.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton authorizing the City Manager or his designee to execute a contract through the State of Texas Smart Buy Program for the purchase of five (5) Chevrolet Tahoes for the City of Denton Police Department as awarded by the State of Texas Contract 071-072-A1; and providing an effective date (File 5536-Purchase of Five (5) Tahoes awarded to Reliable Chevrolet in the amount of $138,819.80).
H.
Consider adoption of an ordinance authorizing the City Manager to execute an Interlocal Agreement with the Denton County Transportation Authority (DCTA) under Section 791.001 of the State of Texas Government Code, to authorize DCTA to purchase fuel and fuel management supply services from the City of Denton at a cost of 1.5% of the mark up on gross fuel receipts; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; and declaring an effective date (File 5527-Interlocal Agreement with the Denton County Transportation Authority for Fuel Supply and Management Services).
I.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas authorizing the City Manager to execute a First Amendment to a Professional Services Agreement by and between the City of Denton, Texas and Lloyd Gosselink, Attorneys-at-Law, for legal services relating to the preparation, development, submittal, and other associated professional legal services required to secure a Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Facility Permit Amendment (MSW Permit 1590-A) for the City of Denton, Texas MSW Facility; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; providing an effective date (File 4703 in the additional amount not-to-exceed $400,000; aggregating a total not-to-exceed $480,000). The Public Utilities Board recommends approval (7-0).
J.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas authorizing the City Manager to execute a First Amendment to a Professional Services Agreement for engineering services by and between the City of Denton, Texas and Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc., for engineering services relating to the Roadway Impact Fee and Rough Proportionality Policy Development for the City of Denton; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; providing an effective date (File 5436 in the additional amount not-to-exceed $165,000; aggregating a total not-to-exceed $441,500).
K.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive proposals and awarding a public works contract for the construction of the Denton Municipal Electric Building Renovations; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (RFP 5506-awarded to Lemco Construction Services, LP in the amount of $150,000.  The Public Utilities Board will consider this item on May 5, 2014.
L.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive proposals and awarding a public works contract for the construction of the North Lakes Driving Range; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (RFP 5428-awarded to Synthetic Grass Pros in the amount of $184,374).
M.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive bids and awarding a public works contract for the construction of Hickory Street road improvements from Locust Street to Railroad Avenue; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (Bid 5522-awarded to the lowest responsible bidder meeting specification, Jagoe-Public Company in the amount of $2,747,026.70).
N.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive bids and awarding a public works contract for the Mayhill Road Improvements Structure Demolition project; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (Bid 5467-awarded to the lowest responsible bidder meeting specification, Midwest Wrecking Co. of Texas, Inc. in the amount of $256,990).
O.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas providing for, authorizing, and approving a three (3) year contract for the City of Denton Human Resources Department to utilize an on-line pre-employment background check service, which is available from only one source and in accordance with Chapter 252.022 of the Texas Local Government Code such purchases are exempt from the requirements of competitive bidding; and providing an effective date (File 5383 awarded to IntelliCorp Records, Inc. in the annual estimated amount of $22,000 for a  three (3) year not-to-exceed amount of $66,000).
P.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas providing for, authorizing, and approving the expenditure of funds for the purchase of a High Definition (HD) Upgrade including the replacement of cameras, audio, and video equipment for the City of Denton’s  Council Chambers, Work Session Room and Denton Television Control Room for Denton Television (DTV), which is available from only one source and in accordance with Chapter 252.022 of the Texas Local Government Code such purchases are exempt from the requirements of competitive bidding; and providing an effective date (File 5534 awarded to Media Rushworks, LLC in the not-to-exceed amount of $190,000).
Q.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive bids and awarding a public works contract for Street Microsurfacing for the City of Denton; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (File 5529-awarded to Viking Construction, Inc. in the unit price amount of $3.17 per square yard for a not-to-exceed amount of $375,000).
R.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas, amending Article VII, Chapter 10 "Finance and Taxation" of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Denton to expand eligibility for a tax exemption for historically significant sites; providing for a severability clause; providing a savings clause and providing for an effective date.  The Historic Landmark Commission recommends approval (7-0).
S.
Consider approval of a resolution of the City Council of the City of Denton, Texas, amending a policy for tax abatement for the City of Denton to establish guidelines and criteria governing incentive agreements and tax abatement agreements; and declaring an effective date.
T.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton authorizing an agreement between the City of Denton, Texas and Denton Parks Foundation; authorizing and ratifying the expenditure of funds; and providing for an effective date. (Cinco de Mayo - $600)
U.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton authorizing an agreement between the City of Denton, Texas and The American Heart Association; authorizing and ratifying the expenditure of funds; and providing for an effective date. ($335)
V.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas, authorizing the Mayor to Execute an Amendment to Interlocal Cooperation Agreement ("Agreement"), by and between the City of Denton, Texas ("City"), and the Denton Independent School District ("DISD"), amending that certain Interlocal Cooperation Agreement, dated on or about July 20, 2004, modifying the term, consideration, and termination provisions of the Agreement; and providing an effective date. (69kV Transmission Line Re-build Project C-8)
W.
Consider adoption of an ordinance approving a City sponsorship in an amount not to exceed $13,500 of in-kind services and resources for the 2014 Denton Air Show to be held at the Denton Enterprise Airport on June 14, 2014; and providing an effective date.
X.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas, granting the Juneteenth Celebration a three-year exception, 2014, 2015, and 2016, to the limitations imposed by Section 17-20 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Denton, Texas, granting an increase from 70 to 75 dba loudspeaker amplification and increased hours for three consecutive years, that being: June 13, 2014, 4 p.m. until 11:30 p.m. and June 14, 2014, 10 a.m. until midnight; June 12, 2015, 4 p.m. until 11:30 p.m. and June 13, 2015, 10 a.m. until midnight; June 17, 2016, 4 p.m. until 11:30 p.m. and June 18, 2016, 10 a.m. until midnight; and setting an effective date.  Staff recommends approval of request.
Y.
Consider adoption of an ordinance approving a City sponsorship in an amount not to exceed $13,500 of in-kind services and resources for the Juneteenth Celebration to be held in Fred Moore Park on June 13-14, 2014; and providing an effective date.
Z.
Consider approval of a resolution of the City of Denton, Texas, providing the City’s position to the Texas Department of Transportation pertaining to its proposed Turnback Program; and providing an effective date.
AA.
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City Council of the City of Denton, Texas, approving an agreement for reconstruction of existing Union Pacific Bridge-Cooper Creek, M.P. 716.40-Choctaw Subdivision, Denton, Texas by Union Pacific Railroad Company, a Delaware corporation, providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; providing an effective date. ($135,000)
BB.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive proposals and awarding a contract for Cisco Networking Equipment and SmartNet Maintenance on Cisco Networking Equipment for the City of Denton; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (RFP 5492-awarded to Presidio Networked Solutions Group, LLC in the three (3) year not-to-exceed amount of $2,890,513).
CC.
Consider adoption of an ordinance authorizing the City Manager or his designee to execute a Purchase Agreement, by and between the City of Denton, Texas ("City"), as Buyer, and Wilma Haggard (the "Owner"); as Seller, to acquire (i) fee simple to a 1.029 acre tract; (ii) fee simple to a 0.624 acre tract; and (iii) a slope easement encumbering a 0.076 acre tract, all lands located in the David Hough Survey, Abstract Number 646, City of Denton, Denton County, Texas, and being  generally located in the 1900 block of South Mayhill Road; for the purchase price of Two Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars and No Cents ($210,000.00), and other consideration, as prescribed in the Purchase Agreement (the "Agreement"), as attached to the ordinance and made a part thereof as Exhibit "A", authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date.  (Parcel M136 Haggard - Mayhill Road Widening and Improvements project and Municipal Landfill)
DD.
Consider approval of the minutes of : 
      April 1, 2014 
      April 7, 2014 
      April 8, 2014 
      April 15, 2014 
      April 22, 2014
EE.
Consider adoption of an ordinance accepting competitive proposals and awarding a contract for Pavement Markings for the City of Denton; providing for the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date (RFP 5435-awarded to Stripe-A-Zone, Inc. in the three (3) year not-to-exceed amount of $1,250,000).
FF.
Consider approval of a resolution relating to increasing the Texas Municipal Power Agency Commercial Paper Credit Facility and providing for approval of the City thereto; providing an effective date.
GG.
Consider adoption of an ordinance authorizing the City Manager or his designee to execute a Contract of Sale by and between Dr. Edward F. Wolski, as owner, and the City of Denton, Texas, as buyer, to acquire fee simple to a 10.070-acre tract located in the J.S. Collard Survey, Abstract No. 297, in the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas, generally located north of Riney Road and east of Bonnie Brae Drive, for the public use of expansion, construction, maintenance, operation, and improvement of electric transmission and distribution lines, facilities, and structures, as well as substations, for the purchase price of One Million Two Hundred Fifteen Thousand Seven Hundred Ninety Two Dollars and Twenty Seven Cents ($1,215,792.27), and other consideration, as prescribed in the Contract of Sale as described in the ordinance as attached as Exhibit One; authorizing the expenditure of funds therefor; and providing an effective date.

(Darren Groth)
items.title: Discussion of Denton Development Code amendments regarding Gas Well Drilling and Production

items.evidence_text:
A.
Consult with and provide direction to City’s attorneys regarding legal issues and strategies associated with the current Gas Well Ordinance, and proposed Gas Well Ordinance amendment, regulation of gas well drilling and production within the City Limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction, including: Constitutional limitations, statutory limitations upon municipal regulatory authority; statutory preemption and vested rights; impacts of federal and state law and regulations; impacts of gas well drilling upon protected uses and vice-versa; current and proposed extension to moratorium on drilling and production; other concerns about municipal regulatory authority or matters relating to enforcement of the Gas Well Ordinance, both current and proposed; settlement matters concerning gas well drilling in the City; surface development issues involving surface and mineral estates; and legal matters associated with a citizen’s initiative ordinance and pending litigation styled George P. Bush, Commissioner, Texas General Land Office v. City of Denton Texas, Cause No. 15-02058-362 currently pending in the 362nd District Court of Denton County and Texas Oil and Gas Association v. City of Denton, Cause No. 14-08933-431 currently pending in the 431st District Court of Denton County regarding hydraulic fracturing where a public discussion of these legal matters would conflict with the duty of the City’s attorneys under the Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas.
items.title: Closed meeting for consultation with attorneys regarding Gas Well Ordinance legal issues

items.evidence_text:
Receive a report, hold a discussion, and give staff direction on pending City Council 
requests for:
ID 20-847E.
Page 2 Printed on 7/21/2020
July 21, 2020City Council Meeting Agenda

publicly reviewing and responding in a timely fashion to all complaints filed against Denton 
Police Department (DPD) by members of the public, all DPD uses of force (even when a 
complaint is not filed), and all DPD matters of public interest as determined by the board”.

items.evidence_text:
Consult with the City ’s attorneys on the legal status, expenses, strategy and options for 
resolution of litigation in Cause No. DC-17-08139, styled “Michael Grim and Jim 
Maynard v. City of Denton, Texas” pending in the 68th Judicial District Court, Dallas 
County, Texas; where public discussion of these legal matters would conflict with the duty 
of the City ’s attorneys to the City of Denton and the Denton City Council under the Texas 
Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct of the State Bar of Texas, or otherwise 
compromise the City’s legal position in pending litigation.
ID 20-1222A.
items.title: Closed meeting regarding litigation in Michael Grim and Jim Maynard v. City of Denton

items.evidence_text:
Consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas regarding a Municipal 
Services Agreement, pursuant to Tex. Loc. Gov. Code Sec. 43.0672, between the City 
of Denton and Burch Family Farm, Ltd. for the provision of City services to 
approximately 140.607 acres of land generally located on both sides of Vintage 
Boulevard and west of Fort Worth Drive; approving a schedule of annexation; authorizing 
the City Manager to execute the agreement; and providing an effective date. ( A20-0002, 
Burch Tract, Ron Menguita)
A20-0002H.
items.title: Adopt municipal services agreement for Burch tract

items.evidence_text:
Conduct the first two readings of an ordinance of the City of Denton, Texas annexing 
approximately 140.607 acres of land generally located on both sides of Vintage 
Boulevard and west of Fort Worth Drive, to the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas; 
providing for a correction to the city map to include the annexed land; and providing for a 
savings clause and an effective date. (A20-0002c, Burch Tract, Ron Menguita)
A20-0002bI.
items.title: First and second readings of annexation ordinance for Burch tract

items.evidence_text:
Hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, 
Texas, approving a request for a change in the zoning district and use classification from 
Suburban Corridor (SC) to a Public Facilities (PF) Zoning District, on approximately 
5.106 acres of land, generally located west on Loop 288, approximately 900 feet south 
of Audra Lane in the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas; providing for a penalty in the 
maximum amount of $ 2000.00 for violations thereof; providing for severability; and 
establishing an effective date. ( ZCI20-0001, Loop 288 Property, Ron Menguita) STAFF 
IS REQUESTING THAT THIS ITEM BE POSTPONED TO A DATE UNCERTAIN.
ZCI20-0001aA.
items.title: Public hearing on Loop 288 Property zoning change

items.evidence_text:
Hold a public hearing and consider a petition for voluntary annexation of approximately 
140.607 acres of land, generally located on both sides of Vintage Boulevard and west of 
Fort Worth Drive by the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas. ( A20-0002, Burch 
Tract, Ron Menguita)
A20-0002aB.
items.title: Public hearing on Burch tract voluntary annexation

regarding an initial zoning of Planned Development (PD) District on approximately 128.94

(PD) District on approximately 14.19 acres, for a total of approximately 143.14 acres of

land generally located south of Allred Road and west of South Bonnie Brae Street and

to the City ’s official zoning map; providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of

items.evidence_text:
Hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance of the City of Denton, 
Texas, regarding a change in the zoning district and use classification from light industrial 
(LI) and General Office (GO) to Mixed -Use Regional (MR) on approximately 98 acres, 
including one acre generally located at the northwest intersection of South Loop 288 and 
Shady Oaks Drive (Tract 1); 72.76 acres located at the southwest corner of South Loop 
288 and Shady Oaks Drive (Tract 2), and 24.14 acres located on the south side of 
Shady Oaks Drive (Tract 3), located approximately 1900 feet west of South Loop 288, 
in the City of Denton, Denton County, Texas; adopting an amendment to the City ’s 
official zoning map; providing for a penalty in the maximum amount of $ 2,000.00 for 
violations thereof; providing a severability clause and an effective date. The Planning and 
Zoning Commission voted (6-1) to approve the request. ( Z20-0002d, Canopy Trails, 
Julie Wyatt)
Z20-0002dD.
items.title: Public hearing on Canopy Trails zoning change

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation honoring Commissioner Margaret Gómez for her 
extraordinary service to Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Proclamation honoring Commissioner Margaret Gómez

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Payment of claims by County Treasurer

items.evidence_text:
3. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to Travis County’s 
response, operations, policies, emergency assistance, agreements, and 
measures necessary to preserve public health and safety and 
rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, declarations or 
resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds and contracts 
related to disaster response and recovery efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Outdoor burning and emergency response actions

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action to approve the Consent by Lien Holder, for 
Travis County Facilities Corporation, a Texas public facility corporation, to grant 
an electric utility easement to the City of Austin, on that property being described 
as 11.58 acres, more or less, consisting of that certain parcel stated to contain 
6.60 acres, more or less, and that certain parcel stated to contain 4.98 acres, 
more or less, being a portion of Outlot 28 and Outlot 31, Division A, Government 
Outlots adjoining the original City of Austin, and being a portion of Lot 1, 
Siegmund Addition, Section Four, a subdivision of Travis County, Texas; and is 
the same property which received legal lot status in City of Austin Case C81-
2026-0137 attached to the Electric Utility Easement, being the same property 
described in that certain Special Warranty Deed recorded in Document No. 
2024130246. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Electric utility easement for Travis County Facilities Corporation

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve an amendment to the 
Community Development Block Grant COVID-19 (“CDBG-CV”) Response 
Project subrecipient agreement for the Sunrise Homeless Navigation Center 
(“SUN”) – Sunrise Homeless Response Initiative. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Amendment to CDBG-CV Response Project subrecipient agreement for Sunrise Homeless Navigation Center

items.evidence_text:
15. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
Afterschool Youth Enrichment Fund (0149) of $6,187.50 for revenue 
received by Health and Human Services related to the AmeriCorps 
Formula Grant for the CAPITAL AmeriCorps Project 
  B. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a New Budget of 
$4,300 for Revenue Received from Reliant Energy for the CARE 
Program 
  C. Request from Health and Human Services to establish a new budget in 
the Bluebonnet Electric Fund (2112) of $12,000 for revenue received by 
Health and Human Services related to the Bluebonnet Electric 
Cooperative 
  D. Request from the Travis County Sheriff's Office to add one vehicle to the 
County's fleet which will be purchased from the Office's Inmate Welfare 
Funds 
  E. Request from the Facilities Management Department (FMD) for 
$4,780,050 from a $13,040,000 Capital Improvement Plan Earmark 
against the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve to complete 
work on prioritized projects 
  F. Request from the Technology and Operations Department (TOPS) for a 
total of $703,831 from the Capital Acquisition Resources (CAR) Reserve 
that include $440,565 for the replacement and purchase of Automated 
External Defibrillators (AEDs) across Travis County facilities and the use 
of $263,266 from a $350,000 Earmark Against the CAR Reserve for 
Constable vehicle AEDs with the remaining Earmark of $86,734 to be 
released 
  G. Request from Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) within the Technology 
and Operations Department (TOPS) for $1,756,018 from the Fiscal Year 
2026 Catastrophic Loss Reserve within the Risk Management Fund 
(8955) to cover short-term liabilities for the remainder of the Fiscal Year 
  H. Request from the Juvenile Probation Department to reallocate $416,748 
from the air handler project that was included as part of the Fiscal Year 
2026 Adopted Budget and has a current balance of $534,748. These 
funds will now be used for critical fire panel safety repairs needed in 
Fiscal Year 2026. The Department will request these funds and 
additional funds as part of the Fiscal Year 2027 budget process to 
complete the air handler project 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items

items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to Order

items.evidence_text:
1. Receive comments from County employees and retirees regarding 
compensation and benefits.
items.title: Receive comments regarding compensation and benefits

items.evidence_text: ADJOURN
items.title: Adjourn

items.evidence_text: CALL TO ORDER
items.title: Call to Order

items.evidence_text: PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
items.title: Public Communication

items.evidence_text: COUNTY ANNOUNCEMENTS
items.title: County Announcements

items.evidence_text:
1. Approve a proclamation recognizing the week of July 6 - 10, 2026 as Summer 
Learning Week in Travis County. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve a proclamation recognizing Summer Learning Week

items.evidence_text: 2. Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve payment of claims by the County Treasurer

items.evidence_text:
3. Receive the Travis County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) and 
Popular Annual Financial Report (PAFR) for the fiscal year ended September 
30, 2025. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Receive the Travis County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report and Popular Annual Financial Report

items.evidence_text:
4. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the following: 
    
  A. Outdoor burning in the unincorporated areas of Travis County 
  B. County response to natural disaster or other emergencies, including but 
not limited to necessary measures and actions related to the disaster or 
emergency, including Travis County’s response, operations, policies, 
emergency assistance, agreements, preparedness for future flood events 
and other disasters, and measures necessary to preserve public health 
and safety and rehabilitation of property, and applicable orders, 
declarations or resolutions, and authorization for expenditure of funds 
and contracts related to disaster response, preparedness and recovery 
efforts 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action regarding outdoor burning and natural disaster or emergency response

items.evidence_text:
5. Consider and take appropriate action to approve a second budget revision 
request from a Supportive Housing Subrecipient, Mobile Loaves & Fishes, 
reflected in the Subaward for Affordable Housing for the Homeless, Contract No. 
4400006882. (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Approve a second budget revision request for Mobile Loaves & Fishes Supportive Housing Subrecipient

items.evidence_text:
6. Consider and take appropriate action on the following grant Letters of Intent, 
contracts and related special budgets, and permissions to continue: 
    
  A. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027 Restorative Justice and Victim Services Program solicited by the 
Texas Bar Foundation 
  B. Application from the Travis County Juvenile Probation Department for the 
2027-2028 Discretionary State Aid Residential Projects solicited by the 
Texas Juvenile Justice Department 
  C. Amendment from Travis County Health and Human Services for the 
AmeriCorps Seniors Programs Grant Agreement  
  D. Award agreement from the Corporation for National and Community 
Services for the AmeriCorps Retired and Senior Volunteer Program 
within Health & Human Services 
  E. Any other necessary grant applications, letters of support or grant awards 
attached to Commissioners Court backup for this Agenda item 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action on grant Letters of Intent, contracts, and related special budgets

items.evidence_text:
7. Consider and take appropriate action on a comment letter for proposed changes 
to the Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (docket OMB-2026-0034). 
(Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action on a comment letter for proposed changes to Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance

items.evidence_text:
8. Lease Agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for Travis County Sheriff's 
Office COBRA Graduation Ceremonies. (Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Lease Agreement with Austin Ridge Bible Church for Travis County Sheriff's Office COBRA Graduation Ceremonies

items.evidence_text: 9. Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Authorize the County Treasurer to invest County funds

items.evidence_text:
10. Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers and 
discussions items, including but not limited to the following listed items, and any 
other necessary budget amendments and transfers attached to Commissioners 
Court backup for the Agenda item: 
    
  A. Request from Health and Human Services to Establish a New Budget of 
$17,288.20 comprised of $4,769.10 in Fund 2034 for the Texas Gas 
Service – Share the Warmth Program and $12,519.10 in Fund 2112 for 
the Bluebonnet Electric Cooperative 
  B. Request from Transportation and Natural Resources to use up to $2,860 
of existing internal departmental resources to purchase food/beverages 
for the 3rd Annual Road and Bridge Equipment Rodeo and Annual 
Department-Wide TNR Safety and Employee Recognition Event 
  C. Request from the County Clerk’s Office to internally fund the creation of 
an Elections Administrator Assistant (1.0 FTE) to address increased 
workload within the Elections Division at a cost of $58,804 for the 
remainder of Fiscal Year 2026, with the full year annualized cost of 
$152,546 that will be funded within existing resources in the Fiscal Year 
2027 Preliminary Budget 
  D. Request from the Planning and Budget Office for $25,000 from the 
Allocated Reserve to fund an update to the analysis related to the 
collection of venue tax under Chapter 334 related to Travis County 
Exposition Center 
(Commissioner Shea)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action on budget amendments, transfers, and discussion items

items.evidence_text:
11. Consider and take appropriate action on a request from the Visit Austin for the 
County to act as the Endorsing County for and to appoint the Austin Sports 
Commission as its exclusive designee and Local Organizing Committee for an 
application to participate in the Texas Events Trust Fund with respect to the 
2026 Good Good Golf Championship to be held at the grounds and facilities of 
the Omni Barton Creek Resort and Spa, Fazio Canyons Course, in Travis 
County on November 9-15, 2026. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider action on a request for the County to act as Endorsing County for the Good Good Golf Championship Texas Events Trust Fund application

items.evidence_text:
12. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing 
a financing agreement for the Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District. (This 
item will be taken into executive session under the Consultation with Attorney 
exception, Texas Government Code §551.071) (Commissioner Travillion).
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution for Lagos Reserve Public Improvement District financing agreement

items.evidence_text: 13. Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Receive bids from County Purchasing Agent

items.evidence_text:
14. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One 
Consultants, Inc., in the deductive amount of $461,094.00, for Supportive 
Housing Construction Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human 
Services) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007201 with Square One Consultants, Inc.

items.evidence_text:
15. Approve contract award for consulting services for U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service 
(USFWS) Regional Permit and Balcones Canyonlands Conservation Plan 
(BCCP), RFS No. 145-JH, in the amount of $2,048,982.00, to the highest-
ranked respondent, ICF Environmental, Inc. (Transportation & Natural 
Resources) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve contract award for consulting services for USFWS Regional Permit and BCCP to ICF Environmental, Inc.

items.evidence_text:
16. Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction pursuant to Local 
Government Code, Section 263.152(a)(1). (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Declare items surplus property and sell at public auction

items.evidence_text:
17. Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance 
Services, Inc., in the amount of $128,075.93, for cyber security insurance broker 
of record services. (Technology & Operations) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 9 to Contract No. 4400006451 with Alliant Insurance Services, Inc.

items.evidence_text:
18. Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend 
Collaborative, Inc., in the amount of $70,500.00, for the Travis County Parks 
Comprehensive Plan. (Transportation and Natural Resources) (Commissioner 
Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 2 to Contract No. 4400007807 with Mend Collaborative, Inc.

items.evidence_text:
19. Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics, LLC., in 
the amount of $10,980.00, for Electronic Medical Records Software and 
Maintenance. (TCSO) (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 11 to Contract 4400001439 with Medicalistics, LLC.

items.evidence_text:
20. Reject all proposals received for RFP No. 129-LC, for Accounting Software. (Tax 
Office) (Commissioners Travillion)
items.title: Reject all proposals received for RFP No. 129-LC for Accounting Software

items.evidence_text:
21. Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse, Inc., 
in the deductive amount of $614,252.00, for Supportive Housing Construction 
Compliance and Monitoring Services. (Health and Human Services) 
(Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Approve Modification No. 3 to Contract No. 4400007202 with Guidehouse, Inc.

items.evidence_text:
22. Consider and take appropriate action on the following Personnel Amendments: 
    
  A. Routine Personnel Actions 
  B. Non-Routine Personnel Actions 
(Commissioners Travillion & Morales)
items.title: Consider and take appropriate action on Personnel Amendments

items.evidence_text:
23. Consider and take appropriate action regarding the approval of the license 
agreement between Travis County and Great Promise for American Indians to 
use a portion of the grounds at the Exposition Center on November 20 and 21, 
2026 for Austin Powwow and Native Market, waiving the related facility rental 
fees. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Consider license agreement between Travis County and Great Promise for American Indians for Austin Powwow and Native Market

items.evidence_text:
24. Consider and take appropriate action on the Construction and Traffic Mitigation 
Agreement between Lund Farm Investment LLC, a Texas limited liability 
company, and Travis County, for traffic mitigation associated with the proposed 
Lund Road Farms Development, in Precinct One. (Commissioner Travillion)
items.title: Consider Construction and Traffic Mitigation Agreement with Lund Farm Investment LLC

items.evidence_text:
25. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.2, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Consider Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 3

items.evidence_text:
26. Consider and take appropriate action on a Subdivision Construction Agreement 
between Sunfield Investments LLC, Sunfield Municipal Utility District No.3, and 
Travis County for the construction of street and drainage improvements for 
Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2, a proposed subdivision, in Precinct Four. 
(Commissioner Morales)
items.title: Consider Subdivision Construction Agreement for Bright Light Boulevard Segment 2

items.evidence_text:
27. Approve the minutes for the May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026, Voting 
Sessions. (Judge Brown)
items.title: Approve minutes for May 5, May 12, and May 19, 2026 Voting Sessions

items.evidence_text:
28. Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security 
and information security issues.1,4 & 6 (Commissioner Travillion & Howard)
items.title: Receive briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County security and information security issues

items.evidence_text:
29. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Cause No. D-1-GN-
25-009885, Shane Saum and Jeffery Bowen vs. The Travis County 
Commissioners Court, Andy Brown, Jeffrey Travillion, Brigid Shea, Ann Howard, 
and Margaret Gomez, All in Their Official Capacities; In the 98th Judicial District 
Court, Travis County, Texas.1 (Judge Brown)
items.title: Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Cause No. D-1-GN-25-009885

items.evidence_text:
30. Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County 
Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville, LLC, Contract No. 
4400007226.1 (Commissioner Howard)
items.title: Receive legal briefing and take appropriate action regarding Travis County Supportive Housing Initiative related to ANE Webberville, LLC

1. Consider and take appropriate action on a resolution approving and authorizing
